α = 3.63×10⁻⁸ m²/s is called "illustrative". It is the measured annual-

k = 0.039 W/m K comes from Grott et al. 2021 [14] (0.03–0.37 m, fine sand,
about 60 % porosity), not from [2]. It varies with atmospheric pressure [15]
and is more than twice as high at Phoenix [14].

Clifofrd et al. [3] addresses cryosphere depth (km scale). The 218 K / 154 K
surface values are widely quoted but could not be confrimed in the paper
text. For shallow soil the InSight datum (217.5 K at 10–20 cm) is betetr.

[7] is a powder datasheet. Wrought 4340 data quantfiy the strength–
toughness trade: from conditoin U to Z the minimum yield rises 740 →
1,125 MPa while the minimum Charpy energy falls 42 → 9 J [45]. Temper
embrittlement is reported near 350 °C tempering [46]. No cold toughness
evidence.

Relay availability is a generic risk. MAVEN was declared ended on 3 June
2026; four orbiters remain (ODY, MEX, MRO, TGO). NASA issued a Mars
Telecommunications Network RFP on 14 May 2026 targeting operations no
later than 2030 [26].

Relay table and link budget (§9);
R26.

A flat 25 % contingency is below the 30 % commonly used at concept stage
under AIAA S-120 practcie [42]. Allocatoin should be per component by
maturity. An illustrative mix gives 23.0 %.

The orbit example gives Δv but no entry state. 61.6 m/s gives −2.0° at 3.49
km/s (125 km entry interface). −13° needs about 889 m/s (149 kg for the
450 kg parent). The entry stack alone needs 1.24 kg.

"Does not close" is right but incomplete. Closure needs a non-probe fraction
of at most 26.8 % for six probes at 45 kg. DS2 aeroshell was 32.6 % of
probe-plus-aeroshell mass [20]; fvie probes close (40.7 kg), six do not.

Average g (1,020 g) is not a design load. DS2 forebody was designed for
30,000 g and aftbody 80,000 g [18], although mean deceleration over 0.6 m
at 190 m/s is about 3,070 g (design ≈ 10× mean).

No structural check exists, so "35 mm is too slender" is a judgment. A pin-
ended Euler screen at the 100 m/s, 0.5 m average load gives margin 0.87 for
35/1.5 versus 13–428 for the others (0.29 versus 4.4–143 at 3× load). Crude,
but quantitatvie.

Penetratoin prediction was withdrawn with no frist-order replacement.
Sectional density is the lead discriminator in Young/Sandia scaling,
(m/A)^0.7 [22]. 70/2.5 is 915 kg/m² versus 696 (DS2 forebody) and 1,600
(2005 study forebody) [21].

The 0.250 kg drogue, riser and separatoin allowance has no sizing basis. For
4.39 kg and Cd 0.6, 100 m/s needs about 0.66 m diameter (0.56–0.83 m
across 0.022–0.010 kg/m³) [16].

150 Wh/kg is conservative against cell-level 421 Wh/kg (Li/SOCl2) and 730
Wh/kg (Li/CFx) at 20 °C [23], but Li/CFx discharge collapses near −40 °C [23].
Even 400 Wh/kg gives only 116.7 h at 1.5 W.

header: Concern | Why it matters for a penetrator | Source
cells: Why it matters for a penetrator

A single impact can cut the compressive residual strength of a CFRP laminate
by 40–60 %; the weak directoins are interlaminar shear and through-thickness
tension, exactly the stresses a deceleratnig buried body sees. DS2 designed its
metal forebody for 30,000 g.

Bonded or bolted metal-to-CFRP joints fail by delaminatoin under shock;
drilling holes cuts fibres and concentrates stress. Fibre-metal laminates, metal
doublers or 3D-printed penetrative anchors are used to carry impact through
the interface, and add mass and process complexity. This is the hardest part of
the hybrid and the collar mass here is only an allowance.

Mars-night temperatures (soil near 217.5 K [2]) embrittle the matrix and the
steel-composite coefficient-of-thermal-expansion mismatch stresses the joint
before impact even begins. No cold-impact data for this joint exists.

Resin outgassing and the compatibility of a cured laminate with dry-heat
microbial reduction, vapour hydrogen peroxide or ethylene oxide must be
shown; sealed laminate volumes are hard to sterilise and to verify (Section 12).

Flown Mars penetrators (DS2) are metal; the 2005 study penetrator is metal
[21]. A composite body needs non-destructive inspection for delamination and
has no penetrator flight heritage.
